engagement_background.objective: Christianbook engaged Treya Partners to deliver $655K–$1.2M in near-term cost savings across indirect spend while building a best-in-class, data-driven procurement process that supports PE-backed enterprise value creation and future scalability.
engagement_background.scope_summary: The project covers 8-10 indirect spend categories representing roughly $18 M of the $93 M annual spend baseline (e.g., LTL/FTL freight, merchant processing, corrugated and packaging supplies, employee benefits, janitorial, marketing software, Ingram fulfillment). High-spend postage, small-parcel shipping and other low-opportunity areas are out of scope, and very low spend categories may be dropped after initial review.
constraints_challenges: Long-standing incumbent relationships (e.g., packaging and LTL) create sensitivity to competitive sourcing.
Supplier data responsiveness is unpredictable, making line-item usage collection difficult.
Need for unified, company-wide communications to avoid ‘side conversations’ and parallel sourcing activities.
Tight five-to-six-month timeline driven by PE value-creation goals and a mid-February 2025 completion target.
Limited internal procurement bandwidth—functional leads (Logistics, IT, HR, DC operations) must support Treya in addition to day-to-day duties.

procurement_environment.data_availability: 12-month AP spend extract (Jun-2023–May-2024) plus contract files; additional unit-level usage data to be requested directly from key suppliers.
procurement_environment.data_quality_notes: Spend required cleansing and re-mapping (multiple vendor naming conventions, tail spend categorization); some suppliers reluctant to provide detailed usage, resulting in potential data gaps.
